papers.t: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
papers.abs: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.

papers.t: Near Resonance, Less Ordered: Radius and Mass Ordering in Compact Multi-planet Systems
papers.abs: Compact multi-planet systems exhibit a tendency for planetary radii to follow ordered sequences with orbital position, suggesting that these non-random patterns preserve a fossil record of their formation. Here, we investigate whether ordering of planet radii and masses with orbital period is related to proximity to mean-motion resonances. We compare near-resonant and non-resonant systems using complementary rank- and inversion-based measures of ordering, while accounting for differences in planet multiplicity and uncertainties in the measured planetary properties. We find that radii and masses are less monotonically ordered in near-resonant systems than in non-resonant systems, with the primary radius analysis providing stronger evidence than the mass analysis. This result is opposite to the naive expectation that dynamical instabilities should erase the primordial ordering of initially resonant systems and leave non-resonant systems in a more disordered state.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, submitted to ApJ Letters

papers.t: A Universal Ratio Linking Cosmic Expansion and the Growth of Structure
papers.abs: We identify a universal relation between the onset of cosmic acceleration ($z_t$) and the turnover ($z_{\rm pk}$) of the linear growth observable $fσ_{8}$. In a spatially flat $Λ$CDM Universe, these two redshifts obey $R \equiv (1+z_t)/(1+z_{\rm pk}) = 1.1596$, independent of the present matter fraction and the overall expansion and growth normalisations. This provides a new consistency test for $Λ$CDM, linking both background and growth dynamics. We further establish the conditions under which this extends to broader classes of dark energy and modified gravity theories.
papers.comment: 6 pages, three figures. Additional materials are included in supplemental text. Comments are welcome

papers.t: oMEGACat-JWST I.: Project description and photometric data release
papers.abs: Omega Centauri (NGC 5139, $ω$ Cen) is the most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way and the likely stripped nucleus of an accreted dwarf galaxy. Extensive HST observations have uncovered many of its peculiar features, including complex subpopulations and kinematic evidence for an intermediate-mass black hole via central fast-moving stars. High-precision astrometric follow-up is essential to constrain the orbits of these stars. We present oMEGACat-JWST, a deep photometric and astrometric catalog of $ω$ Cen's core and surroundings that extends our previous oMEGACat efforts to near-infrared wavelengths. The superior sensitivity and angular resolution of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide significant astrometric and photometric improvements, particularly for faint stars. Our catalog is based on a custom reduction of NIRCam and NIRISS imaging across three JWST programs extending out to two half-light radii (10'). In total, our catalog contains approximately 677 000 sources. In the region overlapping with oMEGACat, we achieve high relative completeness (> 90% of HST sources recovered) while detecting over 86 000 new sources below HST's detection limit. Astrometric tests demonstrate a single-image precision as good as 0.5% of a NIRCam pixel (0.15 mas) at mF115W=18; at mF115W=23 the precision is still 1 mas. Color-magnitude diagrams based on our data show the well-known split between the primordial Helium and the Helium enriched populations and are particularly sensitive to light-element (CNO) variations of faint stars. oMEGACat-JWST provides the most complete photometric catalog of $ω$ Cen's core to date. Combined with HST data, it enables multi-wavelength subpopulation analyses. Together with future monitoring observations, its high astrometric precision will improve our understanding of the kinematics of the central fast-moving stars in $ω$ Cen.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 11 Figures; Submitted to Astronomy and Astrophysics

papers.t: Combining Pulsar Timing data with MetaPulsar. The linearized timing model
papers.abs: Combining the data of multiple pulsar timing array (PTA) collaborations increases the sensitivity to nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs) and other signals correlated between pulsars. The International PTA (IPTA) has combined such data, but historically these projects have taken many years. We introduce $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a software package that ingests the $\texttt{.par}$ and $\texttt{.tim}$ files of individual data releases, and turns them into single consistent deterministic models for the combined datasets, compatible with both timing packages $\texttt{PINT}$ and $\texttt{Tempo2}$. We validate the method in four ways. First, we show for two pulsars that the linearized timing solution of a combined dataset does not depend on the parameter values in the $\texttt{.par}$. A mild exception is formed by the Shapiro-delay parameters. No combination considered requires a manual refit. Second, for PSR J0613$-$0200 we show that the residuals are explained by the timing model if we take intrinsic red-noise and dispersion-measure processes into account, and that the single-PTA timing posteriors agree with one another and with the combination, except for the parallax. Third, we quantify the consistency of the timing parameters measured by different PTAs with a two-sample tension statistic, for every pulsar that is observed by multiple PTAs. Finally, we carry out a gravitational-wave background search on the direct combination of the NANOGrav 9-yr, EPTA DR1 (v2.2), and PPTA DR2 data releases, the constituents of IPTA Data Release 2 (DR2). The combined dataset is assembled in under two hours, and the recovered amplitude and spectral index of the common process are consistent with the published IPTA DR2 result. With $\texttt{MetaPulsar}$, a joint PTA analysis can be prototyped as soon as the individual collaborations publish their data, instead of after a years-long reprocessing effort.

papers.t: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
papers.abs: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

papers.t: Testing general relativity with galaxy cluster clustering from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys
papers.abs: Deviations from general relativity on cosmological scales have been proposed as possible explanations for dark energy and dark matter. Galaxy cluster clustering offers an independent probe of gravitational growth, benefiting from theoretically motivated halo-bias constraints and complementing cluster-abundance measurements. We analyse a subsample of the largest publicly available spectroscopic galaxy cluster catalogue to date, constructed from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Following our selection cuts, the sample comprises 85 818 clusters at $0.1\leq z \leq0.4$ with $M_{\rm 500c}\gtrsim 6\times10^{13}\,M_\odot$. To enable a robust clustering analysis of this sample, we develop and validate methods for constructing random catalogues and calibrating the effective halo bias. We model the redshift-space two-point correlation function monopole and quadrupole over separations of $10$--$150\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ to jointly constrain gravitational growth and Alcock--Paczynski (AP) distortions, fixing the matter power-spectrum shape to that of a fiducial cosmology. We infer the product $fσ_8$ of the linear growth rate $f$ and the matter power spectrum normalisation $σ_8$, obtaining $fσ_8=0.45\pm0.08$ at an effective redshift of $z_{\rm eff}=0.28$, changing to $0.52\pm0.03$ when excluding baryon acoustic oscillation scales with tight AP priors. Both results are consistent with general relativity within the adopted fiducial cosmology.

papers.t: An Efficient Method for Directly Integrating the Vlasov Equation in Collisionless and Weakly-Collisional Simulations
papers.abs: We describe and test a new numerical method to solve the Vlasov/Boltzmann equation in systems with arbitrary levels of collisionality. The method combines recent ideas to evolve the distribution function (DF) directly in 6+1 dimensional phase-space in a manner which is Lagrangian in both position+velocity. The 'particles' of traditional Monte-Carlo/Particle-In-Cell/N-body (MC/PIC/NB) methods become mesh-generating points defining a volume partition, each of which carries a set of momentum-Lagrangian basis functions representing a local anisotropic momentum DF. The DF is then integrated between cells and bases via a higher-order reconstruction and Godunov-type method, evolving a 10 or 13-moment representation of each basis to ensure manifest mass/momentum/energy conservation. The method allows one to represent arbitrary DFs, including multiple independent streams but also collisional or phase-mixed or thermal distributions (unlike traditional 'moments' or waterbag/tessellation methods), and the cost is bounded to a modest multiplier of MC/PIC/NB costs. We provide an example implementation which uses a spatially-Lagrangian volume partition, second-order reconstruction, and simple set of bases which ensure constant cell masses and couple directly to existing MC/PIC/NB machinery, made public in the code GIZMO. We validate in a series of test problems, demonstrating manifest conservation, Galilean and translation and rotation invariance, and ability to represent complex DFs without spurious dissipation or instability. We discuss applications where this method can have advantages compared to traditional algorithms for simulations of dark matter, stellar, weakly-collisional neutral gas, and particulate/dust dynamics; multiphase/polydisperse flows; cosmic ray and radiation transport/hydrodynamics; and plasma physics.
papers.comment: 31 pages, 20 figures, submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. Comments welcome. Implementation in the public GIZMO code available at http://www.tapir.caltech.edu/~phopkins/Site/GIZMO.html

papers.t: Probing Lorentz-violating electrodynamics with CMB polarization. II. Updated constraints and forecasts for the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD
papers.abs: We update the constraints on Lorentz-violating electrodynamics from the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Within the minimal Standard Model Extension, we consider the renormalizable CPT-odd and CPT-even operators of the photon sector, which source cosmic birefringence and circular polarization, respectively. Combining Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and South Pole Telescope (SPT) temperature and $E$-mode data with $B$-mode measurements from BICEP/Keck, SPT-3G D1 and SPTpol, we constrain the CPT-odd coefficients to $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|<7.75\times10^{-45}$ GeV and $|\mathbf{k_{AF}}|<3.82\times10^{-45}$ GeV at 95% credible level. These are the strongest bounds to date from any probe, and are driven by the SPT-3G D1 $B$-mode data. For the first time in this type of analysis, we also include the Planck PR4 $EB$ spectrum, which yields a mild preference for a non-zero $|k^{(3)}_{(V)00}|$. For the CPT-even coefficient, we find $k_{F,E+B}<5.99\times10^{-32}$. Including the latest circular polarization measurements from the Cosmology Large Angular Scale Surveyor (CLASS) tightens this bound by about 7%. This is the first time that CMB circular polarization data contribute to constraining this coefficient. Finally, we forecast the sensitivity of the Simons Observatory (SO) and LiteBIRD. With linear polarization only, the two experiments are complementary, with SO tightening the CPT-even bound by about 30% and LiteBIRD the CPT-odd ones by 40 to 45%. Exploiting the sensitivity to circular polarization provided by the non-idealities of its half-wave plate, LiteBIRD could also improve the CPT-even bound by more than an order of magnitude.

papers.t: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
papers.abs: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $α$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-κ$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

papers.t: RevolIACT: a longitudinally distributed array of compact AI-driven Cherenkov telescopes for the time-domain sub-TeV sky
papers.abs: Context. The coming decade will be the golden era of time-domain astronomy. In ten years, however, sensitive very-high-energy observations below ~1 TeV may be possible only at the two sites of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Each can observe a source for only a few hours per night. Aims. We quantify the loss caused by this limited coverage and assess whether RevolIACT, an array of compact stand-alone AI-driven stations, can close the gap. Methods. We estimate the sensitivity that a stand-alone station needs to detect important transients seen by current imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (IACTs). We also compute the temporal coverage of layouts of ten to fourteen stations distributed in longitude, and how many of the 4401 Fermi-GBM gamma-ray bursts each layout could have observed when they occurred. Results. For each station, a sensitivity of ~15 % of the Crab flux in one hour above 0.2-0.3 TeV, about three times worse than that of current IACT systems, would suffice for an array to detect most of these transients. With the standard analysis, a telescope with a 5 m diameter mirror misses this target by a factor of 17. With a video vision transformer, it comes within a factor of two in an idealised simulation, and a 6 m telescope within 1.5. Ten to fourteen stations would provide three to four times the temporal coverage of CTAO, averaged over the sky and for the GBM bursts. Fourteen stations can observe most sources around the clock for about two months per year. Conclusions. Temporal coverage, not only flux sensitivity, will limit sub-TeV transient astronomy in the next decade. RevolIACT would complement CTAO. The concept relies on the transformer analysis, which is still young and will improve. The decisive next step is to confirm this performance on real data, with a prototype station.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Submitted for publication. Companion paper: E. Jobst et al., "A transformer analysis lowers the energy threshold and improves the sensitivity of a compact imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope", Submitted for publication

papers.t: A transformer analysis lowers the energy threshold and improves the sensitivity of a compact imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope
papers.abs: Context. A companion study simulated an idealised stand-alone imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescope with a 5 m diameter mirror. A video vision transformer that processes the raw camera waveforms lowered its energy threshold by a factor of three, compared with the standard analysis based on image parameters. Aims. We use realistic photodetectors, compute the differential flux sensitivity, and study how hardware parameters affect the transformer analysis. Methods. With the simulation tools of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory, we compare three photodetector efficiencies (100 %, 50 % and that of the LST-1 photomultipliers) with the transformer and with a standard analysis optimised for each. We then vary the dish diameter, field of view, pulse width and sampling rate. Results. With the LST-1 photomultipliers, the energy threshold is 0.18 TeV with the transformer and 0.73 TeV with the standard analysis. The standard analysis needs a photodetector efficiency of 100 % to match that threshold. The main reason is that the transformer works with events of about 35 photoelectrons in the camera, whereas the standard analysis needs about 200 before image cleaning. A 4 m dish with the transformer is more sensitive at all energies than a 5 m dish with the standard analysis. Dishes of 4, 5 and 6 m diameter give thresholds of 0.38, 0.18 and 0.13 TeV. Sampling the pixel signals at 2 GS/s instead of 5 GS/s raises the threshold to 0.26 TeV, whereas the single-photoelectron pulse width (1-3 ns) matters little. Conclusions. The analysis matters as much as the mirror area and the photodetector efficiency. With the transformer analysis, the idealised 5 m diameter telescope comes within a factor of about four of the sensitivity of LST-1 and MAGIC above 0.25 TeV, although its mirror area is 21 times smaller than that of the 23 m LST-1. This performance should improve substantially in the coming years.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Submitted for publication

papers.t: The long-period central star of planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455
papers.abs: A significant fraction of planetary nebulae have been shown to host short-period binary central stars, but longer period central stars are scarcer. We aim to characterise the central star of the planetary nebula MPAJ1508-6455 which has previously been claimed to be an intermediate-period binary with a period of approximately 12 days. We study archival and catalogue photometry to probe the previously reported photometric variability and binary spectral energy distribution. We use long-term high-resolution spectroscopic monitoring to measure the radial velocity curves of the two components of the central binary, as well as derive their atmospheric parameters. We also undertook kinematical and chemical abundance analyses of the nebula itself. We find that the central binary of MPAJ1508-6455 has an orbital period of more than five years with a large eccentricity. The binary comprises a relatively low temperature sdO-type central star and a spun-up K-type giant companion. The Kiel mass of the central star is approximately half the dynamical mass derived from the radial velocities. While the nebular systemic velocity and inclination are consistent with the radial velocities of the binary, the nebular abundance pattern adds support for a lower mass progenitor which did not experience hot bottom burning (and is thus more consistent with the Kiel mass than the mass derived from the radial velocities). To the best of our knowledge, the central star of MPAJ1508-6455 is only the fourth planetary nebula central star to have a spectroscopically confirmed orbital period longer than one year.

papers.t: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.abs: Context. At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, $E_{\rm cyc}$, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models. Aims. We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at $L_{3-79}\simeq5\times10^{36}$, $4\times10^{35}$, and $6\times10^{34}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. We supplemented these data with Swift/XRT observations and performed broadband spectral analysis of all three states. Results. The high-luminosity spectrum follows a classical cutoff power law, whereas the intermediate- and low-luminosity spectra require two thermal Comptonization components to reproduce their two-hump shape. In the intermediate state, the cyclotron line, first reported at $\sim50$ keV in the high-luminosity state, lies on top of the high-energy hump. We interpret the low-luminosity state as representing stable accretion from a cold disk. IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in A&A

papers.t: StochAXtic: a JAX-Accelerated, End-to-End Differentiable Framework for Gravitational-Wave Backgrounds from Compact Binary Populations
papers.abs: We present \texttt{StochAXtic}, a package for computing the dimensionless energy density spectrum $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ of the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by compact binary coalescences. Rather than sampling binary populations via Monte Carlo, \texttt{StochAXtic} exploits the \emph{scale invariance} of the waveforms: at fixed mass ratio, spins and tidal deformabilities, the waveform depends on the total mass only through the dimensionless combination $Mf$. This allows all computationally expensive waveform evaluations using \texttt{LALSuite} to be performed once and stored in a population-independent lookup table. The subsequent integrals over mass and redshift can then be recast as convolutions and evaluated efficiently using fast Fourier transforms. We further employ truncated singular value decomposition to compress the lookup table, reducing both computational cost and memory requirements. Once the table has been computed and cached, \texttt{StochAXtic} evaluates $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ in a few milliseconds, achieving a relative numerical error below $10^{-3}$ at frequencies up to $1$ kHz. Its results agree with those of \texttt{popstock} within the latter's statistical uncertainties. Implemented entirely in \texttt{JAX}, \texttt{StochAXtic} also provides gradients of $Ω_{\mathrm{GW}}(f)$ with respect to population hyperparameters, enabling its direct integration with gradient-based inference methods including Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

papers.t: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
papers.abs: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 100 to 100,000 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. However, variations in stellar mass and disk size introduce substantial degeneracies, limiting the usefulness of individual line fluxes as tracers of external irradiation. We therefore assess all pairwise line flux ratios, which can significantly reduce these degeneracies, evaluating their correlation with the external field, the magnitude of their change across the FUV range, and predicted ALMA detectability. We identify 135 promising ratios, including several combining strong FUV sensitivity and high detectability with efficient single-tuning ALMA observations. The strongest diagnostics either contrast high- and low-excitation lines of the same or co-spatial species (e.g. CO J=8-7/J=1-0), probing different regions of the photoevaporative wind, or pair an FUV-sensitive wind tracer with comparatively insensitive emission arising closer to the disk (e.g. HCO+ J=3-2/C2H N=3-2). Our results provide a framework for identifying externally photoevaporating systems from spatially unresolved emission and constraining their incident FUV field strengths.

papers.t: Probing the Macroscopic Imprints of Singularity Resolution: Polarization Diagnostics of Rotating ABG Black Holes
papers.abs: Recent observations by the Event Horizon Telescope have revealed important electromagnetic information around the supermassive black holes $\text{M87}^*$ and $\text{Sgr A}^*$, providing experimental supports for investigating physics near the event horizon. In the absence of a complete quantum gravity theory, exploring the observational appearances and polarized images of accretion flows in regularized geometries, and seeking specific observational differences from Kerr black holes, is of value for understanding the singularity problem. Based on backward ray tracing method, this work investigates both the optical and polarimetric observational features of rotating Ayón-Beato-García spacetime with regularization parameter $Q$. It is found that, compared with the Kerr case, the parameter $Q$ leads to a significant contraction of the size of the inner shadow in the observed optical images. This contraction remains visible even after an illustrative Gaussian filter for images observed at a low inclination angle (e.g. $17^\circ$). In the polarized images, we focus on two observables, the electric vector position angles (EVPAs) and the depolarization regions, on the observer's screen. It is found that depolarization regions do not necessarily reside in the vicinity of the bright photon ring in images at high inclination angles (e.g. $83^\circ$), and a multi-branch structure can be observed. Furthermore, the distribution of EVPAs is insensitive to the regularization parameter $Q$ while the morphology of the depolarization regions can be impacted remarkably by $Q$. The results provide possible optical observable characteristics for the rotating regular spacetime.

papers.t: FastSpecFit: Spectrophotometric Modeling of 38 Million Extragalactic Targets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Second Data Release
papers.abs: Optical spectrophotometry provides a direct window into the physical conditions, kinematics, and formation histories of galaxies and quasars. FastSpecFit is an open-source Python software package that forward-models each Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectrum jointly with its broadband photometry, convolving stellar-population synthesis and emission-line templates with each fiber's native spectral resolution. This forward-modeling approach preserves DESI's uncorrelated pixel statistics, fits a typical spectrum in ~0.1 s of single-core time, and scales to tens of millions of objects, with uncertainties estimated via Monte Carlo resampling. FastSpecFit measures stellar velocity dispersions, non-parametric star-formation histories, stellar masses, star-formation rates, dust attenuation, K-corrections, rest-frame magnitudes, and fluxes and equivalent widths for 46 emission lines, including separate narrow and broad components for the Balmer lines. We describe these algorithms in detail, validate the measurements against independent codes, and present the resulting value-added catalog for DESI Data Release 2, which provides spectrophotometric and physical properties for 38 million extragalactic targets at 0<z<4. We also release a companion photometry-only catalog and document the catalogs previously released for the DESI Early Data Release and Data Release 1.
papers.comment: Submitted to AJ; 73 pages, 13 figures, 7 tables

papers.t: A novel method for dust evolution in protoplanetary disks and a new criterion for gap opening
papers.abs: We present the Grain Residence-Time Method (GRTM), a computationally efficient particle-tracking approach for studying dust evolution and trapping in protoplanetary disks. By reconstructing steady-state dust distributions from particle residence times, this method provides a way to obtain radial dust surface density profiles without directly evolving the dust as a fluid. We compare the GRTM with dust profiles computed via standard methods using the $\texttt{FARGO3D}$ code, which models the dust as a pressureless fluid, and find very good agreement over a wide range of parameter space. Finally, we investigate how dust gap formation depends on the planet-to-star mass ratio ($q$) and Stokes number ($\mathrm{St}$), through a parameter study, establishing an empirical criterion for dust gap opening. In doing so, we have discovered a new regime of gap opening for small grains with $St \lesssim 10^{-2}$ and for planet mass well below Jupiter's, which is likely very relevant for gaps seen in ALMA images.

papers.t: Euclid: Quick Data Release (Q1) -- The evolution of the radio-loud AGN fraction-stellar mass relation to z~3 in the Euclid Deep Field North
papers.abs: The incidence of radio-loud active galactic nuclei (RLAGN) and their energetic output via AGN feedback are crucial in understanding the evolution of galaxies and the large-scale structure of the Universe. In the local Universe, the incidence of RLAGN has been shown to correlate strongly with host galaxy properties, particularly stellar mass. Using the large-area survey capabilities provided by Euclid and the LOw Frequency ARray (LOFAR), we present the first study of the RLAGN incidence--stellar mass relation to $z=3.0$. We perform a stringent analysis accounting for cross-matching reliability and stellar-mass incompleteness. In addition, we test the robustness of our results against AGN and host galaxy classification. This yields a sample of $3\,154$ RLAGN in the Euclid Deep Field North, comprising $2\,803$ low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs). We find that the LERG incidence as a function of stellar mass and radio luminosity follows a tight correlation over more than two orders of magnitude in stellar mass to $z=3.0$. The slope of the power-law relation decreases from $γ\approx2.5$ in the local Universe to $γ\approx1.0$ at $z=3.0$, indicating a relative increase in low-mass LERGs at earlier epochs. Separating the LERG population into actively star-forming and quiescent galaxies reveals that quiescent LERGs show a much steeper relation between incidence and stellar mass, with $γ\approx2.5$ compared to star-forming LERGs that show $γ\approx1.5$. However, the relation seems to be independent of whether galaxies are star-forming or quiescent at $z\geq2$, where both populations show relatively flat relations with $γ\approx1.0$. Our results suggest an evolutionary picture in which the LERG population transitions from cold-mode, merger-dominated accretion at earlier epochs to a scenario in which systems require a massive hot halo to fuel the AGN in the local Universe.

papers.t: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
papers.abs: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.
papers.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, presented at the 29th European Cosmic Ray Symposium (ECRS2026)

papers.t: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
papers.abs: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(α, δ)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

papers.t: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.abs: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.
papers.comment: 10 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to A&A

papers.t: Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing Analysis (BADMET)
papers.abs: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) variability is widely recognized as a promising avenue for constraining black hole mass, yet its practical application remains limited. Although the correlation between black hole mass and variability timescale has been extensively investigated, finite observational baselines often lead to systematic underestimation of the timescale, thereby hindering reliable mass estimation for individual sources. To address this limitation, we develop the Black hole ADaptive Multi-relation Mass Estimation based on Timing analysis (BADMET), an extendable framework that provides black hole mass estimates by assimilating multiple mass-related parameters that include variability properties. We show that incorporating the variability timescale improves mass recovery in the simulated sample and enhances agreement with the reference masses in the observed sample, achieving uncertainties of $\lesssim 0.5$ dex even with a single X-ray observation.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ Letters

papers.t: Improved compensation for missing high-order aberrations with multi-frame blind deconvolution and phase diversity techniques
papers.abs: Context. Image restoration with phase diversity (PD) and multi-frame blind deconvolution (MFBD) techniques lead to remarkable improvement in image quality, but is limited by the number of aberration parameters that can be determined. Compensation for the missing high-order modes is needed to further improve image quality, and to compensate for residual straylight. Aims. We aim to improve on methods for compensating missing high-order aberrations previously proposed by Scharmer et al. (2010) and Lofdahl & Hillberg (2022). Methods. The wavefront is divided into a set of low-order aberrations, which are treated individually, and high-order aberrations that are treated collectively. The high-order part of the transfer function is averaged, assuming Gaussian seeing statistics with Kolmogorov turbulence for the individual aberrations. Assuming that their accumulated effect is roughly uniform over the pupil, we obtain a high-order modulation transfer function that is represented with a single free parameter. Results. The high quality of the of the proposed high-order modulation transfer function is verified by calculating the Strehl from random samples of point-spread functions for D/r0 ranging from 4 to 20, where D is the telescope diameter and r0 the Fried seeing parameter. The proposed approximation offers significant advantages over the earlier proposals. Conclusions. The proposed method of compensating for missing high-order aberrations in PD or MFBD image reconstruction can dramatically improve the fidelity of solar images. Variations of the seeing (r0) within a data-set can be compensated for self consistently during PD or MFBD processing, but the average value of r0 must be provided from an external source. The computational cost of implementing this method is marginal.

papers.t: Solar atmospheric gravity wave phase differences: insights from MANCHA simulations and observations
papers.abs: Phase-difference and coherence diagnostics are widely used to identify gravity waves in the solar atmosphere, but their sensitivity to opacity and radiative-transfer effects remains poorly understood. We investigate the robustness of gravity-wave signatures in velocity and temperature diagnostics and their appearance in spectroscopic observables. We perform k-/omega phase-difference and coherence analyses using three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations with the MANCHA code. Diagnostics are evaluated at constant geometrical heights and optical depths. Synthetic Fe I 6173 Å profiles provide bisector velocities, continuum intensities, and line-core intensities. We also analyse high-resolution quiet-Sun observations from the 1-m Swedish Solar Telescope (SST). Velocity diagnostics show similar phase differences and coherence at both sampling levels, including those derived from synthetic and observed bisector velocities, indicating their relative insensitivity to the sampling method. In contrast, temperature diagnostics show stronger and more extended gravity-wave signatures at fixed geometrical height. Synthetic continuum and line-core intensities retain these signatures but exhibit phase differences more closely resembling temperature diagnostics at constant optical depth. SST observations show similar qualitative behaviour, despite quantitative differences. Our results demonstrate that Doppler velocity provides a relatively robust diagnostic of gravity-wave phase propagation, whereas temperature and intensity diagnostics are more sensitive to opacity and radiative-transfer effects. Consequently, the latter may introduce biases in estimates of wave propagation speeds and energy fluxes.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in the Astronomy and Astrophysics journal; 12 pages, 11 Figures. The abstract has been shortened to meet the arXiv character limit

papers.t: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
papers.abs: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.
papers.comment: Proceedings from The Golden Age of Cataclysmic Variables and Related Objects - VII

papers.t: Effects of QCD Equation of State on Cosmological Parameters and Stochastic Gravitational-Waves Spectrum
papers.abs: We investigate the thermodynamic evolution of the early Universe across the QCD crossover and up to the electroweak (EW) scale, emphasizing the systematic impact of the QCD equation of state (EoS) and electroweak degrees of freedom on thermodynamic variables, cosmological parameters, and gravitational-wave observables. Using the HotQCD EoS as a baseline, we employ Gaussian Process (GP) regression to generate ensembles of 1000 thermodynamically consistent EoS samples, each extrapolated to high temperatures with and without EW contributions. For each ensemble, we solve the Friedmann equations to obtain the expansion history and compute gravitational-wave (GW) observables, including the instantaneous spectral tilt $n_{gw}(f)$ and the normalized GW energy density $Ω_{gw}(f)/Ω_{gw}^{\rm rad}$. We find that including the EW sector is the dominant effect across all observables, outweighing differences among QCD baseline models that share the same lattice calibration. In particular, EW contributions drive the EoS toward the radiation-dominated limit earlier, reduce excursions of the speed of sound toward the causality bound, suppress transient fluctuations in the Hubble and kinematic parameters near $t \sim 10^{-5}$ s, and qualitatively change the GW spectrum from a strongly frequency-dependent signal to a flat, suppressed plateau. These results demonstrate that accurate modeling of the electroweak sector is essential for an unbiased extraction of QCD-era physics from the stochastic gravitational-wave background.

papers.t: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
papers.abs: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|β_m|/|β_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

papers.t: Magnetic Flux Eruptions in Magnetically Arrested Disks: Magnetic Reconnection and Bubble Expansion
papers.abs: Using a high-resolution GRMHD simulation of a magnetically arrested disk, we investigate the physical mechanism driving magnetic-flux eruption. The horizon-threading magnetic flux declines mainly in off-equatorial regions, whereas localized hot spots associated with magnetic reconnection appear near the equatorial plane around the onset of flux decline. A non-axisymmetric, magnetically supported low-density structure, which we identify as a magnetic bubble, expands radially and azimuthally within a pre-existing low-density channel in the filamentary accretion flow. Based on these findings, we propose a physical picture linking reconnection, bubble expansion, and horizon magnetic flux decline. The reconnection occurs in the pre-existing low-density channel, and may reconfigure the field and promote bubble expansion. Magnetic-pressure gradients provide broadly distributed outward support for the expansion, while magnetic tension contributes a localized outward force near the equator. Bubble expansion may limit gas replenishment, helping to maintain the low-density region and reduce the total pressure near the equator. This pressure reduction may facilitate equatorward electromagnetic energy transport. In the simulation, the polar electromagnetic energy flux reverses from poleward to equatorward near the onset of the horizon-flux decline. The equatorward transport is concentrated in the bubble sector and carries electromagnetic energy from the off-equatorial magnetosphere to the equatorial region. This energy supply may sustain localized reconnection and plasma heating as the eruption develops.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ; 14 pages, 10 figures

papers.t: Sub-electron noise with a buried-channel DePFET: characterisation of novel DePFET concepts
papers.abs: Depleted P-channel Field Effect Transistor (DePFET) pixel sensors combine Fano-limited energy resolution with fast, low-noise readout and are used in instruments ranging from particle tracking to X-ray astronomy. In this work, two novel DePFET technologies that address the two factors of the signal-to-noise ratio through fundamental changes to the intrinsic design are characterised: a buried-channel design aimed at reducing the limiting low-frequency noise by weakening the coupling between the channel and Si/SiO$_2$ interface traps, and a super-$g_q$ design intended to increase the charge gain by reducing the effective internal-gate capacitance. Their noise and energy resolution were mapped across the transistor bias space, over a wide temperature range (100-260 K) and for integration times of 0.4-9 $μ$s (readout times of 2-19.2 $μ$s per row), and compared with standard DePFETs as developed for the NewAthena Wide Field Imager (WFI). All three variants reach their lowest noise at about 155 K. The buried-channel device achieves an excellent equivalent noise charge (ENC) of 0.96 e$^-$ (at most 0.83 e$^-$ after subtracting the readout-electronics noise), demonstrating sub-electron noise over a complete 64$\times$64 DePFET matrix in a single readout, alongside a power consumption reduction of more than 50%. The super-$g_q$ DePFET shows a 2.6-fold increase in charge gain (about 1100 pA/e$^-$) but exhibits higher total noise due to an excess noise contribution. The results highlight the potential of the novel DePFETs, with the buried-channel technology offering immediate benefits for low-noise applications such as the WFI.
papers.comment: 32 pages, 17 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to JINST

papers.t: Prescription for the rotational and orbital evolution of main-sequence binaries undergoing resonance locking
papers.abs: In intermediate-mass binary stars, dynamical tides may play an important role in the orbital and rotational evolution of the system. One possible channel for long-term angular-momentum exchange is resonance locking, in which the evolution of the orbital and rotational parameters remains coupled to the evolution of the frequency of a resonantly excited oscillation mode. We aim to develop a simple prescription for describing the orbital and rotational evolution of binary systems undergoing resonance locking, and to assess the range of validity of this prescription. Using the asymptotic formalism for high-order gravity modes, we relate the temporal evolution of mode frequencies to the evolution of the orbital and rotational properties of the binary system. We then compare the resulting prescription with full integrations of the dynamical-tide evolution, including the contribution of multiple forcing frequencies. Depending on the type of resonance locking considered, we identify the regions of parameter space in which locking is expected to be possible in terms of orbital separation and rotation rate. We find that resonance locking is favoured in systems with significant spin-orbit asynchronism. When a locking is maintained, the proposed prescription reproduces the main features of the orbital and rotational evolution obtained from full dynamical-tide integrations, without requiring the explicit computation of the complete forcing-frequency spectrum. If resonance locking occurs, the evolution of the binary system can be described by a relatively simple prescription. Comparison with the observed population of binaries containing gamma-Doradus stars suggests that a significant fraction of the sample lies in regions compatible with the expected location of locked systems. Improved characterisation of these systems is required to distinguish resonance locking from alternative explanations.

papers.t: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
papers.abs: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.

papers.t: A comprehensive Sun-as-a-star catalog of interplanetary type-III bursts: Statistics and a framework for stellar exospace weather applications
papers.abs: Decameter-hectometric (DH) type-III bursts, produced by energetic electron beams escaping into interplanetary (IP) space, are often associated with strong soft X-ray (SXR) flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle events (SEPEs). With future DH missions being planned, these intense bursts could provide reliable exospace weather event diagnostics, given the lack of direct stellar IP particle and CME probes. We present a catalog of DH type-III bursts associated with 538 out of 734 $\geq$C5-class flares observed by Wind and STEREO spacecraft during 2006-2025. Independent of the SXR flare strength, the occurrence and Sun-as-a-star emission properties of DH type-III bursts distinguish confined flares, CMEs with and without strong IP shocks, and SEPEs. We find that logistic-regression models combining SXR and type-III properties provide more accurate and well-calibrated CME/SEPE occurrence probabilities than a model based only on SXR parameters. Further, a space weather event probability-estimation model based on physically meaningful, scale-free parameters derived from SXR and type-III properties outperforms an SXR parameter-only model. This result presents a way to define solar-calibrated exospace weather prediction models extendable to stellar flares with a range of energy scales but similar underlying physics. We also present a catalog of 26 shock-associated type-III (S-type-III) bursts that appear to start from cotemporal DH type-II bursts and are generally associated with fast halo CMEs and major SEPEs. Our catalogs and the scale-free model form a benchmark for exospace weather studies.

papers.t: FILOS: a solar Filament Oscillation Simulator
papers.abs: We introduce FILOS, a solar Filament Oscillation Simulator designed to validate methods for inferring filament dynamics from H-alpha observations. FILOS constructs synthetic filaments from measured spines populated with three-dimensional dipped threads containing hydrostatic plasma. It computes H-alpha optical depth, projects the structure onto the image plane, applies the Global Oscillation Network Group (GONG) instrumental response, and embeds the result in observed GONG background sequences. Independently prescribed damped longitudinal and transverse motions can be imposed; longitudinal periods can also be calculated from thread curvature and prominence height using the pendulum model. In a representative longitudinal experiment, thread periods range from 44.2 to 87.6 min (median 60.8 min). Normalized Lomb-Scargle power maps recover the dominant periodicity and a period-halving signature near equilibrium. Time-distance fitting recovers an onset of 19.53 +/- 0.23 min for a prescribed 20 min and a collective period of 57.71 +/- 0.35 min. Differences from input thread-level values reflect projection, image formation, and progressive dephasing. FILOS also supplies segmentation masks and opacity-weighted plane-of-sky velocity fields, enabling controlled tests of oscillation analysis, observational biases, segmentation, and motion estimation.
papers.comment: Intensity/velocity_video.mp4 refer to images 3 and 7. The ones with appendix in the name refer to the same figures for the experiment presented in the appendix

papers.t: Planet Formation in a Warped Disc: Gravitational Instability and Misaligned Infall
papers.abs: We perform three-dimensional smoothed particle hydrodynamics simulations to investigate the impact of misaligned infall on a gravitationally unstable protoplanetary disc. The interaction between the disc and the infalling gas does not occur uniformly across all radii. As infall impacts the outer disc first, the outer disc experiences stronger torques than the inner disc, resulting in a warped disc where the angular momentum vector of the disc varies with radius. The surrounding infalling gas reprocesses stellar irradiation and re-emits it back towards the disc, resulting in a warmer disc. The higher temperatures cause the disc to become more gravitationally stable resulting in weaker spiral arms. However, over time, infall also continuously increases the disc mass, gradually altering the local conditions and strengthening gravitational instabilities despite the azimuthally averaged Toomre $Q$ indicating that the disc is stable against gravitational instability. Eventually, one of the spiral arms fragments, forming a giant planet by gravitational instability in a disc warped by misaligned infall. Hence, the impact of infall on gravitational instability in general will vary depending on the infall and disc properties due to the balance between the stabilising and destabilising effects. We also find that infall alters the expected signatures of gravitationally unstable discs by introducing asymmetries in scattered-light, continuum, and molecular line emission.

papers.t: Using the 0i Einstein equation to break dark-sector degeneracies
papers.abs: Over the past decade, cosmological observations have started to challenge the $Λ$CDM model. If these tensions persist, they immediately raise one fundamental question: what new physics could be responsible for them? More specifically, do these deviations arise from a modification of gravity, from an evolving or clustering dark energy component, or from dark matter properties beyond the cold dark matter paradigm? In this paper we show that, with current methods, any observed deviation can always be attributed to more than one sector, preventing us from determining if the tension is due to gravity, dark energy or dark matter. The main reason is that current tests rely on unobservable quantities. These quantities are then either related to observables by assuming the validity of specific equations, or compared with theoretical predictions computed within a given class of theories. Both approaches inevitably break the model independence of the tests, leading to degeneracies between gravity, dark energy, and dark matter. To overcome this limitation, we construct a set of three tests that rely only on observable quantities and that, when combined, can distinguish between the three sectors. We show that the $0i$ Einstein equation -- which is never tested in standard analyses -- adds crucial information to that provided by the gravitational slip equation and the Euler equation.

papers.t: Dual and Binary AGN at Cosmic Dawn: The need for a JWST Program to resolve the merger channel of Early Black Hole Growth
papers.abs: The discovery with JWST of accreting black holes (BHs) at z=4-9 in numbers far exceeding pre-JWST expectations, many of them overmassive relative to their hosts and linked to the enigmatic Little Red Dots (LRDs), raises the question of how early BHs form and grow. Hierarchical assembly predicts that galaxy mergers drive gas to galactic nuclei and bring BHs together, leaving a direct observational signature: dual AGN at tens of kpc separations and sub-kpc to few-kpc "duets" in post-merger galaxies, which are the progenitors of the low-frequency GW sources targeted by pulsar timing arrays and LISA. JWST has opened the window to study these systems at z>3. However, these early discoveries are very limited number and come from heterogeneous, largely serendipitous samples, so these systems can hardly be used for robust statistical studies. Within the Genesis initiative We propose a uniformly selected census of dual AGN and their hosts from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn, as a science case for the Genesis initiative. Our tiered strategy uses the survey imaging and spectroscopy for candidate selection at no extra cost, followed by NIRSpec IFU confirmation, multi-band NIRCam (and MIRI/ALMA) host characterisation, and multi-epoch revisits. Confirming and characterising about 100 pairs requires of order 1000 hr, well beyond the ceiling of standard TAC programs, and demands multi-cycle continuity. The census will deliver pair fractions as functions of redshift, separation and luminosity, BH masses and mass ratios, host properties and environments, and the empirical anchor needed to turn merger models into realistic LISA rate forecasts.
papers.comment: MCT Concept White Paper, Genesis initiative, comments are welcome

papers.t: Instantaneous Spectral Bandwidth of Solar Type III Radio Bursts in the Interplanetary Medium
papers.abs: Magnetic reconnection during solar flares accelerates electron beams that generate type III radio bursts through the plasma emission process. Their instantaneous spectral bandwidth is commonly interpreted as a measure of the spatial extent of the emitting population, yet contributions from viewing angle and radio-wave propagation remain poorly constrained. We investigate bandwidths of 20 type III bursts observed by Parker Solar Probe between 0.15-6.5 MHz. The bandwidth increases with frequency and is consistent with previous measurements up to 100 MHz. For the first time, simultaneous observations from multiple spacecraft show similar bandwidths despite large differences in viewing geometry. We further examine bandwidth contributions from intrinsic emission and propagation effects using numerical and analytical simulations, showing that the beam spatial extent is larger than required to explain observed bandwidths, while the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation produces electromagnetic emission bandwidths near the observed lower limit. Temporal broadening due to radio-wave scattering can increase the bandwidth by causing emission from different frequencies to overlap in time. This effect depends strongly on turbulence level and becomes increasingly important for faster electron beams and narrower intrinsic emission profiles. The results demonstrate that observed type III bandwidths cannot be interpreted solely in terms of physically emitting regions: the intrinsic emission bandwidth follows the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation, while propagation-induced temporal broadening provides an additional contribution that can reconcile intrinsic and observed bandwidths. Accounting for radio-wave propagation effects is essential when using type III burst bandwidths to infer the spatial properties of their emitting electron populations.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 10 figures. Accepted in The Astrophysical Journal

papers.t: A branchless single-precision Voigt approximation for spectral synthesis
papers.abs: The Voigt function is evaluated repeatedly in spectral synthesis, and several widely used implementations carry an absolute error floor. We construct QLG, a family of branchless, single-precision approximations, separable in the damping parameter $a$. QLG is named for its three ingredients: Lorentzian and Gaussian generators $L$ and $G$, and an envelope $q$ that multiplies every fitted correction and vanishes at both endpoints. The leading Lorentzian wing amplitude is fixed analytically. Three members reach observed maximum full-profile relative errors of $6.5\times10^{-3}$, $9.2\times10^{-4}$, and $7\times10^{-5}$ over $a\in[10^{-9},10^{9}]$ and $|v|\le10^{5}$. Extended-domain and randomized checks support these error levels. For the tested SIU, MOOG, and Humlicek w4 implementations, the relative error instead approaches 100% towards small values of the damping parameter. We compare synthesis-weighted costs on an Apple M1 and an AMD EPYC 9554 using gfortran 15, and propagate errors through solar-dwarf, red-supergiant, and M-dwarf syntheses. The least expensive member costs 0.98-1.05 times as much as the tabulated Synspec kernel on the M1 and 1.11-1.20 times as much on the EPYC, with a maximum flux error smaller by a factor of 3.6. The intermediate member costs less than every tested arithmetic kernel and holds the flux error below $10^{-3}$. The most accurate member costs 1.6-3.0 times less than w4 and gives 3.4-5.0 times smaller maximum flux errors in the tested syntheses.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf. 10 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. Fortran module implementing the QLG members included as ancillary file

papers.t: Properties of Chromium and Manganese in Tycho's SNR with XRISM/Resolve
papers.abs: The X-ray emission of young supernova remnants gives access to the composition and spatial distribution of elements ejected in supernovae. The emission from the ejecta provides crucial insights into the explosion mechanism, especially for Fe-group elements formed in the innermost layers of the star. The objective of this paper is to provide constraints on the supernova progenitor and explosion mechanism of Tycho's type Ia supernova remnant by studying the properties of Cr and Mn. The unprecedented spectral resolution of XRISM/Resolve allows us to detect significant emission lines of Cr and Mn in different regions of Tycho's supernova remnant, even at small scale, providing a much more precise spatial distribution of Cr and Mn with respect to previous measurements. Significant Cr and Mn emission lines are observed in the Fe bright northeastern-to-southeastern emitting rim, some in the center region, but none in the southern region. The observed mass ratios of Mn/Fe, Cr/Fe and Mn/Cr, are consistent with 1D delayed detonation models of near-Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia supernovae and 1D pure-detonation models of 1 Msol sub-Chandrasekhar-mass progenitors. In both cases, the observations imply supersolar zero-age main-sequence progenitor metallicities. Overall the best agreement is found for models with a too high metallicity to be realistic for Tycho's location. This points to additional sources of neutronisation such as carbon simmering for Chandrasekhar mass progenitor. For sub-Chandrasekhar mass, double detonation models with a WD mass lower than 1Msol are suggested.
papers.comment: Accepted on A&A, 14 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables

papers.t: Unveiling the mutual inclination distribution in astrometric surveys
papers.abs: Mutual inclination in three (or more) body systems (triple stars, circumbinary planets, multi-planetary systems, etc.) is a tracer of their formation and evolution. Gaia Data Release 4 will provide for the first time a catalog of orbital solutions for three-body systems. Because astrometry is only sensitive to the motion in the plane of the sky, there is a degeneracy in the orbital solutions leading to two possible solutions for the mutual inclination in three-body systems. We propose a hierarchical Bayesian framework to circumvent this degeneracy and unveil the mutual inclination distribution in the population. We tested our methods on simulated datasets, and showed that it reliably recovered the injected mutual inclination distributions in various cases. The method is thus promising for the statistical analysis of Gaia DR4 three-body systems.

papers.t: QPO constraints on the rotating Fan-Wang spacetime
papers.abs: In this work, we investigate a rotating regular black hole described by the Fan-Wang solution, which arises from nonlinear electrodynamics coupled to gravity. We examine the motion of neutral test particles along circular equatorial orbits and derive the corresponding orbital parameters, including the angular velocity, specific angular momentum, and specific energy. By perturbing these orbits in the radial and vertical directions, we calculate the associated fundamental epicyclic frequencies. We then employ the relativistic precession model to interpret the observed quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs) in terms of these frequencies. We numerically determine the radii of the innermost stable circular orbits and perform Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations to constrain the spacetime parameters. Using observational and theoretical estimates of the black hole mass and spin parameter from the literature, together with theoretically motivated priors on the Fan-Wang parameter, we obtain the best-fit parameter values. The inferred black hole mass, spin parameter, and QPO emission radii are consistent with the corresponding estimates reported in the literature. Furthermore, the dimensionless Fan-Wang parameter satisfies $l/M < 8/27 \approx 0.296$, in agreement with its theoretical upper bound.

papers.t: Relativistic tidal excitation of g- and i-modes in neutron star binaries
papers.abs: When the gravitational wave frequency of an inspiraling binary matches a normal-mode frequency of a neutron star (NS), the mode can be resonantly excited. The excitation transfers orbital energy to the star and shifts the phase of the emitted gravitational-wave (GW) signal, thereby providing a potential probe of the NS interior. However, estimates of this phase shift in the literature vary by orders of magnitude due to different approximations and formulations used in calculating the tidal coupling strength. We revisit this problem using a fully relativistic scattering formalism, which serves as our benchmark calculation and provides a gauge-invariant mode response together with an effective tidal-mode coupling strength. We calculate the phase shifts induced by the excitation of stratification g-modes, crustal interface i-modes, and hadron-quark interface i-modes, and estimate their detectability with Fisher-matrix forecasts for current and next-generation detectors. In our models, direct g-mode excitation remains below the detection thresholds, even for the strongest stratification considered. Crust-core i-modes at large shear speeds provide the most favorable prospects and crust melting can produce a substantially larger phase shift. Hadron-quark i-modes remain below the next-generation detection thresholds.

papers.t: Probing Velocity-Dependent WIMP Dark Matter Annihilation in Large-Scale Structure
papers.abs: The unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) provides a promising avenue for probing the cosmological annihilation of weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter through its cross-correlation with large-scale structure (LSS). While most previous studies have assumed a velocity-independent (s-wave) annihilation cross section, many well-motivated particle physics models predict annihilation rates that depend on the relative velocity of dark matter particles. In this work, we develop a generalized halo-model framework to investigate the cosmological signatures of velocity-dependent WIMP annihilation. Parameterizing the velocity-weighted annihilation cross section as $σv_{\rm rel}\propto v_{\rm rel}^{n}$, we consider four representative cases corresponding to Sommerfeld-like (n=-1), s-wave (n=0), p-wave (n=2), and d-wave (n=4) annihilation. We show that velocity dependence modifies not only the overall annihilation emission but also the halo population dominating the signal, leading to distinct effective halo biases, redshift distributions, and angular clustering properties. As a result, different annihilation mechanisms leave characteristic signatures in the UGRB-LSS cross-correlation that cannot be captured by the overall gamma-ray intensity alone. As an illustration of the formalism, we perform a statistical forecast for the cross-correlation between the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) UGRB and the Two Micron All Sky Survey Redshift Survey (2MRS) galaxy catalog and derive the projected sensitivities to the velocity-independent annihilation coefficient for these four annihilation scenarios. Our results demonstrate that cosmological cross-correlations provide a powerful and complementary probe of velocity-dependent dark matter annihilation, offering a new avenue for constraining the particle physics of dark matter through its imprints on large-scale structure.

papers.t: Low-frequency Radio Observation of the Dark PeVatron LHAASO J2108+5157 Using uGMRT. II
papers.abs: We present deep radio observations of the PeVatron candidate LHAASO J2108+5157 using the upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT). Our observations reveal a persistent double-lobed radio source (\gmrtext) within the vicinity of the $\geq$100 TeV $γ$-ray emission region, with consistent morphology across 400 MHz, 650 MHz, and 1.2 GHz. No alternative particle accelerators, such as supernova remnants or pulsar wind nebulae, are identified in the region, making \gmrtext\ the most plausible counterpart candidate. We measure the flux and spatially resolved spectra of the source using multi-band radio data. The morphology remains stable across all bands, while a comparison of non-contemporaneous observations suggests possible flux variability. From the measured spectra of the lobes the inclination angle of the jet is estimated to be $86.57^{\circ} \pm 1.15^{\circ}$. The multi-wavelength spectral energy distribution is modeled reasonably well with a lepto-hadronic scenario.
papers.jref: Gunindra Krishna Mahanta et al 2026 ApJ 1012 99

papers.t: Bent-tailed radio galaxies as tracers of the intrafilament medium
papers.abs: Bent-tailed radio galaxies have traditionally been associated with, and used as tracers of, the dense intracluster medium. In recent years, however, such sources have also been identified outside of clusters, with only a few discovered in low-density environments of cosmic filaments. Their occurrence in low-density environments remains rare and is still poorly understood. We announce the discovery of bent-tailed radio galaxies in galaxy cluster filaments. We have identified two bent-tailed radio galaxies, J0020-25 and J0019-26, within a filament at the redshift of $z \sim 0.1273$, and another bent-tailed radio galaxy, J0019-25, in a separate filament at $z \sim 0.1126$. We used MeerKAT observations of these bent-tailed radio galaxies to place constraints on their intrafilament medium (IFM). The effects of the filaments could be seen in the radio morphologies of these galaxies. Using faint regions in each galaxy, we estimate the intrafilament pressure, density, magnetic field strength, and total energy density. We found an IFM density of $ρ_\text{IFM} \approx 3.8\times 10^{-29}$ g cm$^{-3}$ for the surrounding medium of J0020-25 and J0019-26, and $ρ_\text{IFM} \approx (0.2 - 1.1) \times 10^{-26}$ g cm$^{-3}$ around J0019-25.
